On 7th May 2025 at the United Nations in Geneva, Switzerland, Kenya accepted 7 key recommendations from the Civil Society Movement on Sexual Reproductive Health and Rights thematic area during the 4th cycle of the Universal Periodic Review (UPR) process.

The coalition contributed to the UPR Shadow Report, recommending the implementation of the Eastern and Southern Africa Ministerial Commitments for age-appropriate and inclusive CSE for adolescents and young people

2021: This advocacy initiative includes holding strategic meetings at the national level with non-state actors to follow up on the 3rd cycle of UPR recommendations for Kenya on SRHR and gender justice.2022: National advocacy initiatives include re-drafting and tabling of the Reproductive Healthcare Bill of 2019, review of National Adolescent Sexual and Health Policy, reintroduction of RH Bill in parliament, and collaboration in SRHR-related TWGs2023 (first half): This includes progress tracking of ICPD+25, FP2030 country commitments, Family Reproductive Health Bill, etc.

2023 (second half): Total 6. This includes drafting the national AYSRHR policy implementation roadmap, Kisumu County Public Participation Policy and Mombasa Disability Mainstreaming Policy, etc.2024: Total 15. This includes development and submission of memo to national assembly on Population and Developm Bill (NCPD) and international events such as HRC, UPR shadow report. 2025: Total 9. This includes participation in conferences like 8th RHNK Pan-African AYSRHR Scientific Conference and 59th HRC session, as well as submission of memos to the National Femicide TWG and the Gender and Equality bill.

2023 (second half): (1) In October 2023, The Kisumu County Assembly passed The Kisumu County Public Participation Policy 2023, which introduced a chapter on meaningful youth participation (MYP) and inclusivity of minority groups. (2) On 9th October 2023, the Nairobi County Government revised Finance Bill 2023/24 abolishing fees for contraceptive services at the health facilities in the county as had earlier been proposed in the draft bill. 2024: (1) In April, 2024 Kisumu County, through the County Assembly Health Committee developed The Draft Kisumu SRH Bill 2024 (at second reading).The proposed act of the County Assembly will provide for the right for its citizens including adolescents and young people access to reproductive health care; improve standards of sexual and reproductive health;and provision for the right to make own decisions regarding reproductive health.2025: None this year.
